segments.text: Islamic finance seeks to structure financial activity through Shariah-compliant contracts rather than interest-based lending.

Study basic modes such as murabaha, mudarabah, musharakah, ijara and salam/istisna at an introductory level. Takaful is a cooperative risk-sharing model used as the Islamic alternative framework to conventional insurance structures.

blocks.text: How Islamic banking differs in structure

segments.text: Islamic banking seeks to provide financial intermediation through transactions structured to comply with Shariah requirements. Instead of treating every financing arrangement as an interest-bearing loan, institutions may use sale, lease, partnership or agency structures. This changes the legal form and allocation of asset ownership, risk and return, although practical products still require scrutiny of their real substance.

The State Bank of Pakistan regulates Islamic banking institutions through a dedicated framework. Its revised Shariah Governance Framework issued in November 2024 took effect from 1 January 2025, and SBP continues to issue Shariah-related regulations and instructions. Current examination answers should therefore rely on the latest SBP material rather than older descriptions of the regulatory model.

Murabaha is asset-based sale financing; ijarah is lease-based financing; diminishing musharakah combines co-ownership with gradual purchase of one party’s share; salam and istisna support certain forward or manufacturing transactions; mudarabah and musharakah are participation-based structures. Their risks and accounting consequences differ, so the phrase “profit-and-loss sharing” does not describe all Islamic banking.

For each mode, ask: Who owns the asset? Who bears which risk? What is being sold or leased? When does payment become due? What event creates the institution’s return? These questions reveal the legal mechanism.

Takaful is an Islamic insurance model organized around mutual contribution and risk sharing rather than the conventional transfer of risk for a premium. Participants contribute to a fund from which covered losses may be paid, while an operator manages the arrangement under a recognized contractual model.

The practical legal form differs among jurisdictions and products. A good answer explains the mutual-risk concept, governance of the fund, operator’s role and Shariah supervision, then compares these features with conventional insurance without claiming that every conventional insurance contract is identical.

items.text: Islamic banking seeks to structure financing through sale, lease, partnership or other Shariah-compliant arrangements rather than treating money lending at interest as the universal financing method.

Murabaha is a sale in which cost and profit are disclosed; ijara is lease-based; mudarabah separates capital provider and entrepreneur/manager roles; musharakah is partnership participation; salam and istisna address particular forms of future delivery or manufacture.

Each mode should be studied through a transaction diagram: who supplies capital or asset, who owns the asset, when ownership or possession changes, how profit or rent arises, and who bears which commercial risk.

Takaful is built around cooperative risk sharing and participant contributions under a managed structure. Its conceptual difference from conventional insurance should be explained through structure rather than slogans.

rows: Common confusion to avoid: Do not call every Islamic banking product “profit-and-loss sharing.” Some structures are sales or leases and allocate risk differently.

items.text: Prepare each mode with parties, asset/capital flow, profit/rent and main risk.

Use current SBP/SECP material for Pakistan-specific regulation if needed.
